A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, component ablations and conflict analyses across five document-understanding datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds a synthetic annotation-noise experiment and statistical tests.

M1.justification: The C&P Link Tokens, positive and negative C&P Connector samples, training-data construction and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. The noise experiment evaluates a hypothesis without modifying the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use DocVQA, DUDE, DeepForm, FUNSD and ChartQA with the same OCR and cognitive tasks. The new training-label corruption experiment remains within this coverage; it introduces no new dataset, population or evaluation task.

E2.justification: The evaluated model roster and corresponding SFT-baseline and component comparisons are unchanged. GPT-4o, Qwen-VL-Max, InternVL2-2b, InternVL2-8b and Qwen2.5-VL-7b retain their respective roles.

E3.justification: v3 adds an InternVL2-2b experimental protocol with synthetic OCR/VQA annotation noise affecting 5%, 10% and 20% of training data, alongside a 0% control. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and stated fine-tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.5 add a focused annotation-noise sensitivity study for InternVL2-2b to investigate the proposed origin of C&P conflicts. Existing component ablations, conflict-pattern analyses and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: v2 contains no formal significance tests. v3 introduces two-sided paired t-tests with t-statistics and p-values for consistency, cognitive-task and perceptual-task gains across all five datasets, restricted to InternVL2-2b (Appendix A.9, Table 11). This substantially expands statistical reporting, but adds no seed or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: All nine pre-existing numerical tables retain identical values after matching renumbered tables. New Table 10 reports average consistency of 76.40%, 75.62%, 75.44% and 73.88% at 0%, 5%, 10% and 20% noise; Table 11 adds significance outcomes. These supplement unchanged benchmark findings.

T1.justification: The C&P consistency definitions and method constructions in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. Added justification for choosing OCR and VQA does not alter the mathematical formulation; no proofs or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: identifying C&P conflicts, evaluating their prevalence, and mitigating them through consistency fine-tuning while improving task performance.

C2.justification: Section 3 incorporates the noise intervention into the argument linking heterogeneous annotations to conflicts. Section 5.5 newly clarifies that the selected InternVL2-2b/8b examples have identical responses although most other cases differ. The stated applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 specifies corruption types and rates for the added noise experiment. It also removes v2's promise that all constructed data will become publicly available, without supplying replacement access information. Existing hyperparameters, model snapshots and appendix prompts are retained; actual resource withdrawal is not established.

R1.justification: v3 adds MME and PCA-Bench citations supporting the OCR/VQA task choice and several document, web and table references in Section 6, while removing Rabinovich et al. (2023). The central positioning relative to hallucination and knowledge-conflict research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 expands affiliations and contact information, adds acknowledgments and two appendix subsections, and makes localized explanatory and wording edits, including correcting 'qualitative' to 'quantitative' in Section 3. Most prose and the main section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is enlarged and rearranged, with a recolored consistency chart and a new noise-response panel; the previous conflict-pattern panel is retained as panel c. Two result tables are added, and existing figures, tables and appendix prompts are relocated or renumbered within the retained layout style.

improvement.justification: The controlled noise experiment supplies useful evidence for an explanation that v2 supported mainly through error inspection, and the revised Figure 2 improves readability. Benefits are limited by the new analyses covering only InternVL2-2b, incomplete statistical documentation, and Table 11's inconsistent FUNSD C&P pair (t=2.36, p=0.00722) for a two-sided t-test. Removing the data-release promise also weakens the reproducibility commitment. The additional evidence nevertheless provides a modest net improvement.
